sections.title: Disability and unpaid care in Stoke-on-Trent
sections.lede: How many people are limited by a disability or long-term health problem?
sections.label: Select a local authority area for a personalised look at health, disability and unpaid care

sections.content:
There are just over 10 million people in England and Wales whose day-to-day activities are limited by a long-term health problem or disability, while just over 2.1 million people are providing at least 20 hours a week of unpaid care for someone else.

This article uses data from the 2011 Census to show how the numbers vary from area to area.

sections.title: How Stoke-on-Trent compares on long-term health problems and disability
sections.content: In 2011, around 18% of the population of England and 23% of people in Wales were limited, either a little or a lot, in their day-to-day activities because of a long-term health problem or disability.

sections.caption: Proportion of people with long-term health problems

sections.content:
In Stoke-on-Trent, it was almost 57,000 people or 23% of the population.

This is a visually hidden description for screen readers.
This includes 29,000 people (12%) who said their day to day activities were limited a lot.
And this is how the percentage for Stoke-on-Trent compares to all of the local authorities in the West Midlands, where it had the highest percentage.
In England, just over 4.4 million people (8.3%) were limited a lot while in Wales it was just over 360,000 people (11.9%).

sections.title: Disability and long-term health problems are most prevalent in Wales and the north of England
sections.content: The highest percentages of people with a disability or health problem that limited them a lot in their day-to-day lives were recorded in parts of Wales and the north of England.

sections.caption: Proportion of people with long-term health problems

sections.content: This is a map showing the proportion of people with a disability or health problem that limited them either a little or a lot, from low to high.
The highest was in Neath Port Talbot, where 28% of the usual population had a disability or health problem. This is down from 29.4% a decade earlier.
The lowest was in Wandsworth, where 11.2% of the usual population had a disability or health problem in 2011, down from 13.4% in the 2001 Census.

sections.title: One in 26 people are caring for someone unpaid for at least 20 hours a week
sections.content:
In the 2011 Census, data showed that just over 12,000 people (4.8%) were caring for someone else for at least 20 hours a week in Stoke-on-Trent.

This compares with almost 11,000 (4.5%) in 2001.

Across England in 2011, almost 2 million people, 3.7% of the population, provided at least 20 hours a week of unpaid care to someone else. This is up from 3.1% in 2001.

In Wales, it was almost 160,000 people, around one in 19 of the population (5.2%), up from just over 130,000 (4.6%) in 2001.

sections.caption: Proportion of people caring for someone else

sections.content: This is a map showing the proportion of people caring for someone else, unpaid, for at least 20 hours a week in 2011, from low to high.
The highest was in Neath Port Talbot, where 7.1% of the usual population provided at least 20 hours a week of unpaid care. This is up from 6.2% a decade earlier.
The lowest was in the City of London, where 1.6% of the usual population provided at least 20 hours a week of unpaid care in 2011, down from 1.8% in the 2001 Census.

Across England and Wales, just over 2.1 million people (3.8%) provided unpaid care for 20 hours or more a week, with almost 1.4 million (2.4%) providing 50 hours a week or more.

In Stoke-on-Trent in 2011, just over 7,800 people (3.1%) were caring for someone else, unpaid, for at least 50 hours a week.

Neath Port Talbot had the highest percentage in Wales of people providing 50 hours or more unpaid care per week, around 5%. In England, the highest percentage was around 4% in East Lindsey.

This compares with just 1% in the City of London, the lowest in England, and 3% in Cardiff, the lowest in Wales.
